variables.name: factory
variables.comment: the Jar file factory. It handles both retrieval and caching.

variables.comment: the url for the Jar file

variables.name: permission
variables.comment:
the permission to get this JAR file. This is the actual, ultimate,
     * permission, returned by the jar file factory.

variables.comment: the url connection for the JAR file

methods.name: public void setRequestProperty(String key, String value)
methods.comment: * Sets the general request property. * * @param key the keyword by which the request is known * (e.g., "accept"). * @param value the value associated with it.

methods.name: public String getRequestProperty(String key)
methods.comment:
* Returns the value of the named general request property for this
     * connection.
     *
     * @return  the value of the named general request property for this
     *           connection.

methods.name: public void addRequestProperty(String key, String value)
methods.comment: * Adds a general request property specified by a * key-value pair. This method will not overwrite * existing values associated with the same key. * * @param key the keyword by which the request is known * (e.g., "accept"). * @param value the value associated with it.

methods.name: public Map<String, List<String>> getRequestProperties()
methods.comment:
* Returns an unmodifiable Map of general request
     * properties for this connection. The Map keys
     * are Strings that represent the request-header
     * field names. Each Map value is a unmodifiable List
     * of Strings that represents the corresponding
     * field values.
     *
     * @return  a Map of the general request properties for this connection.

methods.name: public void setAllowUserInteraction(boolean allowuserinteraction)
methods.comment: * Set the value of the allowUserInteraction field of * this URLConnection. * * @param allowuserinteraction the new value. * @see java.net.URLConnection#allowUserInteraction

methods.name: public boolean getAllowUserInteraction()
methods.comment: * Returns the value of the allowUserInteraction field for * this object. * * @return the value of the allowUserInteraction field for * this object. * @see java.net.URLConnection#allowUserInteraction

methods.name: public void setUseCaches(boolean usecaches)
methods.comment:
* Sets the value of the useCaches field of this * URLConnection to the specified value. *

* Some protocols do caching of documents. Occasionally, it is important * to be able to "tunnel through" and ignore the caches (e.g., the * "reload" button in a browser). If the UseCaches flag on a connection * is true, the connection is allowed to use whatever caches it can. * If false, caches are to be ignored. * The default value comes from DefaultUseCaches, which defaults to * true. * * @see java.net.URLConnection#useCaches

methods.name: public boolean getUseCaches()
methods.comment: * Returns the value of this URLConnection's * useCaches field. * * @return the value of this URLConnection's * useCaches field. * @see java.net.URLConnection#useCaches

methods.name: public void setIfModifiedSince(long ifmodifiedsince)
methods.comment: * Sets the value of the ifModifiedSince field of * this URLConnection to the specified value. * * @param value the new value. * @see java.net.URLConnection#ifModifiedSince

methods.name: public void setDefaultUseCaches(boolean defaultusecaches)
methods.comment: * Sets the default value of the useCaches field to the * specified value. * * @param defaultusecaches the new value. * @see java.net.URLConnection#useCaches

methods.name: public boolean getDefaultUseCaches()
methods.comment:
* Returns the default value of a URLConnection's * useCaches flag. *

* Ths default is "sticky", being a part of the static state of all * URLConnections. This flag applies to the next, and all following * URLConnections that are created. * * @return the default value of a URLConnection's * useCaches flag. * @see java.net.URLConnection#useCaches
